"Platonic Space: brief argument and research agenda" by Michael Levin
https://t.co/sqC5llToTE

We don't have "full access" to anything :-) (in 3rd person science, anyway).  That's ok, we can still make tons of progress.  Our actual research agenda on this issue is listed at about 16 minutes in of https://t.co/plYzj3h650.  Just to focus on one aspect of it here: exactly how much (and what kind) of "free lunch" do we get from this space?  It's clear that when we make physical interfaces, we get more than we put in. How much more, and what do we get - static patterns, dynamic behavioral policies, algorithms, virtual machines, something else? All of these are different and we can quantify them. In biology it's hard to do exactly (because you don't have a full accounting of the physical interface, and someone can always say "well there's more there you just don't know about yet, maybe quantum something-or-other") but in minimal computational systems, it's more tractable. Stay tuned for that, more coming next year.  And then all the questions I listed in that slide - understand the contents and distribution of patterns from that space, and characterize the mapping between interfaces and the patterns they enable. Lots of experiments to do!
